title: Custom No-Gi BJJ Uniform: A Competition Specification Guide for Gyms and Brands
seoTitle: Custom No-Gi BJJ Uniform Specification Guide | TONTON
description: Learn how to specify a custom no-gi BJJ uniform, from IBJJF checks and rash guard fit to shorts, artwork, sampling, care labels and reorder control.
answer: A custom no-gi BJJ uniform combines a rash guard and grappling shorts with coordinated artwork and separate garment specifications. Define the intended event and rule edition first, then approve fit, materials, seams, measurements, labels and a physical sample. Keep the approved size chart, artwork revision and quantity allocation for bulk production and reorders.
author: TONTON

basis: Based on TONTON product and sampling references and official IBJJF, FTC and AATCC information checked November 20, 2026. Event requirements and manufacturing choices are identified separately.

sections.title: What should a custom no-gi BJJ uniform include?
paragraphs: A practical custom kit normally includes two linked garments:

The two pieces should look like one team system, but they should not be treated as one identical construction. A rash guard needs next-to-skin stretch, seam comfort, and torso coverage. Shorts need secure waist control and movement through shots and scrambles.
TONTON supports the development of custom sublimated rash guards and BJJ/MMA shorts as separate product specifications while coordinating artwork, colors, sponsor placement, labels, and packaging.
bullets: A close-fitting rash guard with an agreed sleeve length, body coverage, fabric direction, seam construction, artwork, and size chart.
Grappling shorts or compression shorts with an agreed length, waistband, closure, pocket treatment, side opening, liner, and logo placement.

sections.title: How do you check the rules before designing a competition kit?
paragraphs: First, identify the exact event, division, gender category, and rule set. A gym’s training uniform can be more flexible than a competition uniform, and one organization’s requirements may not apply to another.

The IBJJF uniform page describes elastic, close-fitting rash guards that cover the torso to the shorts waistband, with specified base and rank colors. For men’s shorts, it gives a half-thigh-to-knee length range and restrictions on pockets, exposed drawcords, zippers, buttons and hazardous hard parts. Check the complete division-specific wording before approving the garment.

Rule timing matters. As checked November 20, 2026, IBJJF also publishes a separate 2027 change notice effective January 1, 2027. Record the event date and applicable edition in your artwork and sample approval. An announced future change is not the rule for every current event.

sections.title: How should you specify the custom BJJ rash guard?
paragraphs: Start with the user and movement pattern rather than the graphic. A team that trains several times a week may need a different fit and seam priority from a lifestyle-oriented private-label brand.
Record these decisions in the brief:

TONTON’s custom rash guard development page identifies a supplied 220 GSM, 85% polyester / 15% spandex reference for one product direction, while making clear that final composition, weight, hand feel, and stretch are confirmed for the selected project. One reference specification should not be copied into every style without approval.
bullets: Short sleeve or long sleeve
Adult, youth, or separate women’s fit direction
Chest, torso, shoulder, sleeve, and hem measurements
Desired compression level and stretch direction
Fabric composition and weight to be confirmed for the selected style
Flatlock or other seam construction to be reviewed on the sample
Optional mesh placement, if required and appropriate for the design
Optional silicone hem grip, including width and placement
Neck label, care label, sponsor marks, and packaging

sections.title: What should you check on the rash guard sample?
paragraphs: Wear-test the garment through pummeling, shrimping, bridging, framing, and repeated overhead movement. Check whether the neckline stays comfortable, the torso remains long enough, the sleeves restrict reach, and seams feel smooth against the skin. If a hem grip is included, check ride-up, skin contact, stretch, and wash performance before approving it as a selling point.

Do not describe a mesh panel as “breathable” in a technical or tested sense unless you have evidence for that claim. A mesh appearance shows construction; it does not prove a measured moisture or airflow result.

sections.title: Which grappling shorts construction should you choose?
paragraphs: Choose shorts according to use, coverage, and rule constraints before finalizing the artwork. The following comparison is a development framework, not a claim that one style is best for every athlete.

TONTON’s high-split 2-in-1 grappling shorts reference shows one direction using a four-way-stretch outer shell and a supplied 250 GSM milk-silk liner reference. Confirm the actual liner composition, weight, length, waistband system, side split, and event suitability on the approved project sample.

sections.title: What artwork and branding information should a team provide?
paragraphs: A strong artwork pack reduces revisions and makes repeat orders easier. Provide vector logo files, brand colors, academy and sponsor hierarchy, front/back/sleeve/side-panel placements, event restrictions, label artwork, packing requirements, and the final artwork revision number.

Review artwork at panel seams, side openings, sleeve joins, waistbands, and curved areas. A design that looks correct on a flat mockup may need adjustment when it is cut and assembled. Keep the approved mockup and physical sample together; the image alone does not define fit or construction.

sections.title: What should the sampling and MOQ checklist contain?
paragraphs: Before asking for a quote, prepare the same information for every supplier:

TONTON’s sampling and MOQ guide states that selected custom projects start from 10 pieces, while also explaining that the applicable minimum depends on style, design, colorway, size allocation, and project requirements. Its advertised 3–7 day sample target begins after usable artwork and product details are confirmed; sourcing, new patterns, and revisions can change the schedule. Use the written quotation, not a generic starting number, as the commercial reference.

Quantity by style, color, and size

Fabric and construction priorities

Destination country and target delivery date
Sample requirements and expected revision rounds

sections.title: How should private-label brands handle labels and care claims?
paragraphs: Private-label sellers should treat labels as part of product compliance and customer experience. Confirm fiber content, country-of-origin requirements, brand identity, size information, care instructions, and market-specific obligations with the responsible compliance professional or importer.

For covered U.S. apparel, FTC guidance calls for attached care instructions supported by a reasonable basis. Review the finished garment and its components when agreeing washing, drying and ironing directions. Consult the official rule and compliance guidance for the product and market.

For sublimated or dark-colored fightwear, agree any required test method and acceptance criteria before making durability claims. AATCC TM15 summarizes acid-perspiration colorfastness testing; a published method is not proof that this garment was tested or that it resists every kind of fading.

sections.title: Key takeaways
bullets: A custom no-gi BJJ uniform is a specification system, not just a matching print.
Check current event rules before approving rash guard colors, torso coverage, shorts length, pockets, drawstrings, zippers, and hard components.
Treat the rash guard and shorts as coordinated but separate constructions.
Approve a physical sample for fit, movement, seams, materials, artwork, labels, and finishing.
Record the final measurement chart, tolerances, artwork revision, material record, packaging, and care instructions for repeat orders.
Use supplier starting points such as MOQ and sample timing as project-specific inputs, not universal promises.

faqs: What is a custom no-gi BJJ uniform?

A custom no-gi BJJ uniform is a coordinated rash guard and grappling-short system developed around a team or brand identity. It should include confirmed fit, materials, construction, artwork, sizing, labels, and intended-use requirements rather than only a printed graphic.
Can a training kit be used in an IBJJF competition?

Not automatically. Training apparel may include design or construction details that do not match current competition rules. Check the official IBJJF requirements and the specific event’s inspection guidance before relying on a kit for competition.
How long should no-gi BJJ shorts be?

For IBJJF men’s no-gi shorts, the official uniform page says they should cover at least halfway down the thigh and be no longer than the knee. Other organizations may differ, so verify the applicable rule set before finalizing the pattern.
Should a rash guard be tight or loose for no-gi BJJ?

A competition-style no-gi rash guard is generally close-fitting and made from elastic material. The final fit should allow full movement without excessive looseness, restricted reach, uncomfortable seams, or insufficient torso coverage.
Are 2-in-1 grappling shorts suitable for every competition?

No. A 2-in-1 construction can be useful for training and grappling movement, but liner color, length, waistband details, side split, and other features must be checked against event rules. Approve the exact garment, not only the product category.
What is a reasonable starting MOQ for custom BJJ gear?

A starting MOQ is project-specific. TONTON states that selected custom projects start from 10 pieces, but the applicable minimum must be confirmed by style, design, colorway, size allocation, and other requirements in the quotation.
Do custom BJJ rash guards need care labels?

Care-label obligations depend on the market and product. For U.S. apparel, the FTC Care Labeling Rule requires covered manufacturers and importers to provide care instructions, and those instructions need a reasonable basis for the finished garment.
What should I send a manufacturer for a custom team uniform quote?

Send garment types, intended use, quantity by size and color, artwork or logos, fit direction, construction priorities, destination country, target date, labels, packaging, and sample expectations. A complete brief produces a more useful project-specific quote.
